semble: not_run (tool not available in the isolated venv)

interpretations.a_decision_set: (a) The DECIDING set is the PRIMARY set: probe45 (45, no flag, all kept) plus the scored trace-derived queries (agent_nav, synthetic_spill and, if present, spill_follow) with every answer_named_verbatim row EXCLUDED, pooled; trivial_head is outside it. It needs n >= 120 AND at least 75 trace rows; with fewer its verdict is UNDERPOWERED/KILL per REPL-EMB-2.1 ('small n kills by design'). The pooled set including flagged rows and the without-synthetic sets are SECONDARY, labelled non-deciding. (Amended 2026-10-20, before any arm ran: first the single spill_follow source yielded n = 0 and the trace stratum became agent_nav + synthetic_spill; then the deciding set became the unflagged one, see (q).)
interpretations.b_registered_hybrids: (b) The kill rule is evaluated for EACH registered hybrid (hybrid-BGE, hybrid-Granite) against L; it PASSES iff at least one registered hybrid passes both conditions (mean diff >= M AND bootstrap CI lower bound > 0). Every individual result is reported. Hybrids over extension arms (EG2, potion) are evaluated afterwards; any changed verdict is flagged extension_only and never replaces the registered verdict.
interpretations.c_selection: (c) The selection rule applies only if the kill rule passed, and uses cpu_s_per_query supplied from the speed block (a JSON file argument). Without it the harness refuses to select and reports 'selection: pending speed block'.
interpretations.d_selection_candidates: (d) Selection candidates are the hybrid arms (registered and extension): the shipped context.search primitive is hybrid by construction, so dense-only, lexical, weighted and ColGREP rows are reported but not eligible. An arm with no cost row keeps selection pending.
interpretations.e_incomplete: (e) A verdict is computed only from arms that scored EVERY deciding query. If L's legs or every registered hybrid are incomplete the verdict is INCOMPLETE, never a pass or fail from partial data.
interpretations.f_pointer_hit: (f) A chunk pointer is (section, start_line, end_line): start = chunk.line; end = line + the number of newlines inside chunk.text after removing exactly ONE trailing newline (a chunk is a run of whole lines, so trailing blank lines stay counted). A pointer hits a query iff it has the same section (path) and overlaps a gold span by >= 1 line.
interpretations.g_probe45_bundles: (g) probe45 bundles, per repo: every *.py under the package root (seaborn/, pylint/, src/_pytest/) plus the gold files if outside it, read from the pinned checkout (HEAD must equal the rows' commit); section = repo-relative path; the shipped chunk_sections(..., 800); the chunk count must be <= 4096 (asserted, recorded).
interpretations.h_code_intent: (h) code_intent (applied only where the input value is null; blind to every arm's output) is True iff the query text matches the regex in CODE_INTENT_REGEX; the labelled file records the source ('input' | 'regex') of every label.
interpretations.i_dense_hybrid: (i) Dense-only and hybrid share ONE query embedding per query: the vector the shipped ContextSearchIndex.search embeds (captured by a delegating wrapper). Hybrid = the hits of idx.search(query, 10, section=None, embedder=adapter); dense-only = idx._dense_ranking(vector, None)[:10]. A search whose meta mode is not 'hybrid' (dense failure, invalid or degenerate vector, timeout, build failure) is a MISS for hybrid AND dense-only and increments n_failed.
interpretations.j_groups: (j) Groups: probe45 rows = group probe45; a trace row's group is its own `stratum` when that is agent_nav, synthetic_spill or spill_follow (any other label = spill_follow, the legacy default, recorded as group_source); the trivial-head files = group trivial_head, scored but reported outside the decision. A row with no gold span is scored:false and excluded everywhere.
interpretations.k_offline_budget: (k) The shipped index-build budget is disabled for the offline eval (INDEX_TIMEOUT_MIN_S = INDEX_TIMEOUT_MAX_S = 1e9) so it cannot censor an embedder; budget exposure belongs to the speed block. Every cost number produced here is flagged contended_not_for_selection.
interpretations.l_weighted: (l) weighted_hybrid (static arms only; reported, non-deciding): score = 0.75/(60+rank_dense) + 0.25/(60+rank_bm25) over the same two 64-candidate rankings; ties break on str(id) as rrf_fuse does; rrf_fuse itself is untouched.
interpretations.m_colgrep: (m) ColGREP is a registered arm on probe45 only (code-only, tree-sitter): the trace bundles (agent_nav, synthetic_spill, spill_follow) are .txt, so it is not_applicable there and is excluded from its n. It is reported against L on probe45 and takes no part in the kill rule.
interpretations.n_sets: (n) Sets: PRIMARY (deciding) = every scored non-trivial row EXCEPT those flagged answer_named_verbatim (probe45 has no flag and is kept whole). SECONDARY, labelled '(non-deciding)': pooled including flagged rows; without synthetic_spill with flagged rows excluded; without synthetic_spill with flagged rows included; each stratum separately (the per-stratum recall tables). A secondary set identical to an earlier one is not repeated. Every set gets its own L (the better of grep / BM25 on it), recall tables and kill-rule evidence with the n floor; the any-passes interpretation (b) applies within each set. Per-stratum paired diffs vs L, recall split by synthetic writer (A/B), and the answer_named_verbatim / intent_source cuts are descriptive and never gate.
interpretations.o_synthetic_bias: (o) Synthetic queries are LLM-written; they tend to share vocabulary with their source span, which favours lexical arms. The synthetic stratum therefore makes the kill rule conservative toward dense arms.
interpretations.p_selection_primary_only: (p) Selection is evaluated for the PRIMARY set only, gated by its own kill verdict; the speed block is shared. Secondary sets get no selection.
interpretations.q_prerun_amendment_primary_unflagged: (q) PRE-RUN AMENDMENT 2026-10-20, before any arm ran: the only deciding set is the PRIMARY set with every answer_named_verbatim row excluded (probe45 + agent_nav, synthetic_spill and spill_follow unflagged). Reason: the pooled set is 81% synthetic and 42% of the synthetic queries are flagged answer_named_verbatim; left in the deciding set, that leakage would let the lexical arm dominate and could kill dense retrieval through a query-writing artefact. The kill rule, L, the floors, selection, the bootstrap tables vs L and vs BGE and the extension-flip logic use the primary set alone; the earlier pooled with/without-synthetic sets stay as secondary, non-deciding reports. Floors, checked at freeze (loud warning) and at analyze (verdict UNDERPOWERED/KILL): primary n >= 120 AND trace rows (non-probe45, non-trivial_head) >= 75. Leakage is measured, not corrected: recall@{1,3,5,10} on the flagged and the unflagged subsets, flag rates by stratum, writer and intent_source.
